prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create one polished character design casting sheet for a mobile fitness app mascot (personal trainer ↔ client app: scheduling, workouts, progress).
Landscape canvas, 4 columns × 2 rows, eight different animal candidates, precisely one full-body character per cell, all in the SAME unified visual style and comparable visual scale. Each in a front three-quarter view and neutral friendly standing pose. Generous even spacing; entire ears, feet and tails visible.
Top row left to right labels: "1 otter", "2 red panda", "3 raccoon", "4 fox".
Bottom row left to right labels: "5 hamster", "6 penguin", "7 capybara", "8 frog".
Each label is small, clean dark sans-serif centered below its character. No other text.
Style built for 2D rig animation in Rive: simple rounded primitive shapes (circles, ovals, capsules), clean vector illustration look, Duolingo-level polish but original designs, no copying Duolingo's owl or existing mascots. Use NO outlines consistently across all eight, except simple dark mouth lines if necessary. Flat fills; no textures, fur strands, gradients, or rendered lighting. At most one soft flat shadow color, no blur.
Per animal: limited palette of 2–3 body colors plus a single small warm orange (#FF7A1F) sporty wristband or headband. Big expressive eyes with clearly visible eyelids, simple mouths; emotion designed to remain readable at 48px. Friendly, confident, slightly playful adult energy, not babyish. Compact slightly bottom-heavy bodies for squash and stretch, short limbs, chunky readable silhouettes, one or two simple follow-through parts (ears, tail, tuft; frog eye lobes and penguin flippers) that could swing in animation. Species identity must remain clear, including otter's rounded ears and tapered tail, red panda's broad ringed tail, raccoon's dark mask, fox's pointed ears and bushy tail, hamster's round cheek silhouette, penguin's flippers and belly, capybara's blunt rectangular-rounded muzzle, frog's raised eyes and broad mouth. Avoid tiny decorative details.
Plain uniform warm off-white background, no frames, no grid lines, no extra props, no title, no watermarks.
refinement:
Refine this casting sheet while preserving the exact 4×2 layout, eight species in order, exact labels, full-body framing, warm off-white background and orange sport accents.
Make one targeted style correction across ALL eight: strictly flat geometric construction suitable for Rive rigs. Remove ALL gradients, tonal modulation, texture and 3D shading from every body part and the background. Each shape must have a perfectly uniform solid fill. Limit each character to 2–3 body fill colors plus orange accent and eyes/mouth dark and white. No cast shadows needed. Replace fur spikes, cheek hairs, whiskers, toe/finger lines, and intricate contours with broad smooth circles, ovals and capsules. Make torsos compact, slightly bottom-heavy, limbs short. Keep clear species recognition and adult confident friendly expressions with big eyes and visible simple upper eyelids, not babyish. No outlines consistently. Labels unchanged, no added text, props or accessories. Otter should have just the headband as its orange detail; others retain one orange sporty detail each. This must look like clean flat vector shape artwork, not shaded digital painting.
note: Exploratory raster casting sheet, not a layered vector or Rive rig. Generated artwork retains some tonal variation and small contour details. Does not supersede the saved lynx mascot choice.
